A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Knowledge Bridger, with matching main methods and experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 includes Supplementary Material G–L; the supplied v5 ends after the references. This is an observable omission from the supplied document, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, component and candidate-count ablations, model-scaling experiments, and qualitative completion and hallucination analyses, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v5 retains original three-dataset experiments, ablations, model-scaling results and generated examples, and adds inference-time measurements in Table 4.

M1.justification: The knowledge extraction, entity-based generation and graph-plus-CLIP/BLIP ranking procedures remain unchanged in Section 2. The omitted appendix provided prompts and ranking pseudocode; its absence does not establish removal of method components.

E1.justification: Both evaluate image/text completion and multilabel classification on COCO-2014, MM-IMDb and IU X-ray. v5 elaborates the IU label construction without establishing different task coverage. Its added reference to appendix results with 'more modalities' supplies no actual additional evaluation.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the complete-data and missing-data-removal baselines, MPMM, MPLMM, MMIN and DiCMoR. Direct generation remains the qualitative comparator in Figure 3. The omitted supplementary comparisons used the same comparator set.

E3.justification: Table 4 adds inference time as an evaluation measure. Section 3.1 revises IU sample accounting from 7,470 images with 756 test samples to 6,674 training and 756 testing samples. Neither this revision nor the mAP-to-AP relabeling establishes that experiments were rerun or that metric aggregation changed.

E4.justification: v5 omits Table 6's additional component ablations at missing rates 0.3 and 0.5, retaining the main 0.7 analysis. Supplementary completion cases, candidate-ranking examples, intermediate knowledge graphs and hallucination cases in Figures 4–10 also disappear. These losses substantially narrow mechanism and failure analysis; Table 4 adds runtime evidence for the existing candidate-count tradeoff.

E5.justification: Both report averages over five random seeds, without confidence intervals or significance tests. v5 omits Appendix H's additional statement that repeated simulations reuse the same missing-sample set. This reduces repeated-run documentation without establishing any change in run count.

E6.justification: Retained main-table accuracy and similarity values and Figure 2 trends remain unchanged. Table 4 adds times of 7, 40, 83 and 132 seconds for 1, 5, 10 and 15 candidates. However, Table 5's IU X-ray comparisons at missing rate 0.5, additional Table 6 ablation results and supplementary qualitative outcomes disappear, substantially reducing reported evidence.

T1.justification: The graph-similarity definition and combined quality-score equations remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs. The omitted ranking pseudocode restates the retained scoring procedure rather than contributing separate theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: training-free, modality-agnostic completion using LMM knowledge, strong general-domain and OOD performance, benefits from knowledge-guided generation and ranking, and improvement with model scale.

C2.justification: Section 5 retains the image/text restriction, hallucination concern and classification-versus-similarity tradeoff. However, omitted Appendix K explicitly connected hallucinations to training-data limitations and reduced task-specific common sense in a training-free approach. That substantive explanation is absent from v5.

D1.justification: Removing Appendices G–H eliminates detailed prompts, output formats, ranking pseudocode, vLLM deployment information, 72B quantization, context/output limits, temperature and missingness-simulation instructions. v5 adds a code-access link, runtime measurements and clearer IU label-construction information, but substantially reduces the reproducibility information contained in the PDF.

R1.justification: v5 adds citations on multimodal prompting, domain adaptation, clustering and lip reading, while removing references including original Qwen-VL, semantic-entropy hallucination detection, vLLM and Lewis et al.'s RAG work. The central positioning against trained MMC methods and diversity-oriented conditional generation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main Sections 1–6 remain largely intact, with localized condensation, terminology edits and a corrected Table 4 cross-reference. However, the entire structured supplement G–L is removed rather than relocated, substantially reducing the explanatory organization. Multiple retained footnotes still direct readers to the absent appendix.

P2.justification: v5 removes supplementary Tables 5–6, Figures 4–10, the prompt panels and Algorithm 1, eliminating substantial visual and tabular documentation. Main Figures 1–3 remain unchanged. Table 4 gains a time column, and metric headers change from mAP to AP.

improvement.justification: The new code link and quantitative runtimes are useful, but the supplied v5 removes detailed prompts and inference settings needed for reproduction, broader ablation evidence and concrete hallucination cases while retaining the core claims. Unresolved appendix references compound the loss. These reductions in reproducibility and critical scrutiny substantially outweigh the limited reporting improvements.
